entries.summary: The Chocolate Hills viewpoint in Carmen looks over Bohol’s distinctive grass-covered limestone hills. The wider geological landscape extends across a large area; this listing identifies the Carmen visitor viewpoint rather than every hill in the province.

Their grass cover changes from green to brown during the dry season, giving the formation its name. This listing concerns the viewpoint in Carmen, a particular place from which to see the landscape. A provincial landscape photograph is useful orientation, while current access to the visitor viewpoint should be checked locally.

entries.summary: Baclayon Church is the Immaculate Conception parish church in Baclayon, Bohol. Its coral-stone building was completed in 1727, giving this active religious landmark a particular place in the province’s church heritage.
overview: The parish commonly called Baclayon Church is dedicated to the Immaculate Conception. Baclayon’s Christian settlement began under Jesuit priests in 1596; the parish was established in 1717 and the present coral-stone church completed in 1727. Augustinian Recollects later took over and renovated the building. The church belongs to the Diocese of Tagbilaran and is located in Baclayon municipality, rather than Tagbilaran City itself.
highlights: Learn the parish’s Jesuit and Recollect history.

entries.summary: The National Museum of the Philippines–Bohol occupies the former provincial capitol in Tagbilaran City. The restored building connects Bohol’s civic history with museum subjects including art, earthquake heritage and natural history.
overview: The former provincial capitol in Tagbilaran was built between 1855 and 1860. Its earlier uses included a tribunal, prison and military quarters before it became the seat of provincial government. The 2013 Bohol earthquake damaged the building; it was later donated to the National Museum, repaired and reopened as a museum in July 2018. The institution describes galleries concerning Napoleon Abueva, the earthquake and Bohol’s natural history. The building’s reuse is part of the visit, alongside the collections. Use the museum’s current information when planning around a particular exhibition.
highlights: Explore the museum’s art and natural-history subjects.
